editions.headline: Frost advisory for low-lying parts of Valley County
editions.text: Temperatures could fall to 28 degrees around Alder Creek and Riverside before sunrise on Thursday, Jan. 2. The weather service advised covering sensitive plants and bringing pets inside.

editions.headline: Minimum wage rises to $16.50 in Calder
editions.text: Calder's minimum wage rose to $16.50 an hour on Jan. 1, up 50 cents under the state's inflation adjustment. Tipped workers receive the same minimum.

editions.headline: Snowpack at 57% of average in January survey
editions.text: Surveyors measured the Calder snowpack at 57% of the long-term average for Jan. 2, the Department of Water Resources said. Officials asked cities to plan for a dry summer.

editions.headline: El Concejo de Punta Brava aprueba la ampliación de la costanera
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 2 de enero por 7 votos contra 1. Las obras comenzarían el año próximo.

editions.headline: Employers added 175,000 jobs in December; unemployment holds at 4.1%
editions.text: Employers added 175,000 jobs in December, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate held at 4.1%. Average hourly pay rose 0.3% from the month before. Part-time work accounted for most of the change.

editions.headline: Taqueria opens on Eastbank's Main Street
editions.text: Grace Muñoz opened a taqueria in Eastbank on Saturday, in a space that had been empty since 2024. It is the third new business on the block this year.

editions.headline: Corte de agua el lunes en Bahía Honda
editions.text: La cooperativa de agua anunció un corte el lunes 6 de enero de 9 a 15 horas entre las calles Sarmiento y Brown de Bahía Honda, por trabajos en la red. Recomendó a los vecinos reservar agua el día anterior.

editions.headline: Alerta por vientos de hasta 84 km/h para el martes
editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 69 km/h para el martes 7 de enero. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre Villa Marina y Puerto Claro, y el puerto demoró la salida de dos buques de carga.

editions.headline: El puerto de Puerto Claro recibió 19 cruceros en diciembre
editions.text: La administración portuaria informó este lunes que 30,761 pasajeros de 19 cruceros desembarcaron en Puerto Claro durante diciembre. Los comerciantes del casco histórico reportaron más ventas que en la temporada anterior.

editions.headline: Valdora coast: puerto de Puerto Claro recibió 19 cruceros en diciembre
editions.text: El Faro del Litoral, the Costa Norte regional newspaper, reported on Monday, Jan. 6: "La administración portuaria informó este lunes que 30,761 pasajeros de 19 cruceros desembarcaron en Puerto Claro durante diciembre." Tallywire translated the report from Spanish.

editions.headline: Stamp price rises to 73 cents on Jan. 19
editions.text: A first-class stamp will cost 73 cents starting Jan. 19, up from 70 cents, the Postal Service reminded customers Tuesday. Forever stamps bought earlier remain valid.

editions.headline: Eastbank names new fire chief
editions.text: The Eastbank City Council confirmed Owen Petrakis, the interim fire chief since spring, as fire chief. Mayor Hollis Grant praised the choice. The council met Tuesday, Jan. 7.

editions.headline: Harbor City approves 68-unit apartment building near the station
editions.text: The Harbor City Council voted 3-1 to approve the project, 13% of whose units will rent below market rate. Neighbors had asked for a shorter building. The council met Tuesday, Jan. 7.

editions.headline: Corte de agua el sábado en Puerto Claro
editions.text: La cooperativa de agua anunció un corte el sábado 11 de enero de 9 a 15 horas entre las calles Colón y Sarmiento de Puerto Claro, por trabajos en la red. Recomendó a los vecinos reservar agua el día anterior.

editions.headline: El Concejo de Puerto Claro aprueba un nuevo plan de residuos
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 9 de enero por 11 votos contra 3. La oposición pidió una consulta popular.

editions.headline: Comienza la temporada de calamar en Punta Brava
editions.text: La flota artesanal de Punta Brava salió el viernes 10 de enero para la apertura de la temporada de calamar. La cooperativa de pescadores espera buenos precios en el mercado regional, aunque el combustible subió un 8% desde 2024.

editions.headline: Transit agency proposes first Valley Line fare increase since 2019
editions.text: Valley Regional Transit staff have proposed raising the base Valley Line fare from $2.50 to $2.75 on July 1, the first increase since 2019. Monthly passes would rise from $80 to $88. The board will hold a public hearing Feb. 11 at the Millbrook headquarters; written comments are due Feb. 7.

editions.headline: Valley Unified weighs closing Pine Hollow Elementary
editions.text: Valley Unified trustees will study closing Pine Hollow Elementary, where enrollment has fallen to 140 students. A decision is expected in March.

editions.headline: Prices up 2.7% from a year earlier in December
editions.text: Consumer prices rose 2.7% in the year to December, down from 2.9% the month before, the Statistics Bureau said Wednesday. Rent and car insurance rose fastest.

editions.headline: Reserve Council cuts key rate to 4.25%
editions.text: The Reserve Council cut its benchmark rate a quarter point to 4.25% at the end of its January meeting on Wednesday, Jan. 15. The council said it would watch the job market closely.

editions.headline: Calder unemployment dips to 5.1% in December
editions.text: Calder's unemployment rate fell to 5.1% in December, the state Employment Department said Friday. Employers added 6,500 jobs; state and local government saw the largest swing.

editions.headline: Bill would limit insurer cancellations in high fire-risk areas
editions.text: Assemblymember Chris Lyle introduced SB 58 on Friday, a bill that would limit insurer cancellations in high fire-risk areas. The governor's office has not taken a position.

editions.headline: Dense fog slows morning commute
editions.text: Visibility dropped below a quarter mile on Highway 9 and in Millbrook on the morning of Saturday, Jan. 18. Fog is expected again Sunday before a dry, cool weekend with highs near 61.

editions.headline: Bill would provide free breakfast in every public school
editions.text: Assemblymember Nadia Farouk introduced AB 219 on Tuesday, a bill that would provide free breakfast in every public school. A similar bill died in committee two years ago.

editions.headline: Harbor City Council delays vote on a plastic bag fee
editions.text: After two hours of public comment on a plastic bag fee, the Harbor City Council postponed its vote to next month and asked staff to meet with neighborhood groups. 23 people signed up to speak. The council met Tuesday, Jan. 21.

editions.headline: Millbrook names new police chief
editions.text: The Millbrook City Council confirmed Imani Brooks, formerly of Cinder Bay, as police chief. Mayor Denise Arceo praised the choice. The council met Tuesday, Jan. 21.

editions.headline: Eastbank approves 83-unit apartment building on the old cannery site
editions.text: The Eastbank City Council voted 4-2 to approve the project, 19% of whose units will rent below market rate. Neighbors had asked for a shorter building. The council met Tuesday, Jan. 21.

editions.headline: Frost advisory for low-lying parts of Valley County
editions.text: Temperatures could fall to 32 degrees around Alder Creek and Riverside before sunrise on Monday, Jan. 27. The weather service advised covering sensitive plants and bringing pets inside.

editions.headline: Bill would raise the state minimum wage to $18 by 2027
editions.text: Assemblymember June Halvorsen introduced SB 301 on Monday, a bill that would raise the state minimum wage to $18 by 2027. The governor's office has not taken a position.

editions.headline: Economy grew at 2.3% rate in fourth quarter
editions.text: The economy grew at a 2.3% annual rate in the fourth quarter of 2024, the Commerce Office said Thursday. Consumer spending accounted for most of the growth.

editions.headline: Corte de agua el sábado en Villa Marina
editions.text: La cooperativa de agua anunció un corte el sábado 1 de febrero de 22 a 6 horas entre las calles Sarmiento y Colón de Villa Marina, por trabajos en la red. Recomendó a los vecinos reservar agua el día anterior.

editions.headline: El Concejo de San Telmo aprueba una tasa turística
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 30 de enero por 10 votos contra 1. Los vecinos podrán presentar objeciones durante 30 días.

editions.headline: Storm to bring 3 inches of rain to the valley
editions.text: A Pacific storm will reach Valley County on the night of Saturday, Feb. 1, with 2 inches of rain expected by Monday. Snow levels will drop to 5,000 feet in the eastern foothills. Highs will stay near 48.

editions.headline: Snowpack at 56% of average in February survey
editions.text: Surveyors measured the Calder snowpack at 56% of the long-term average for Feb. 1, the Department of Water Resources said. Officials asked cities to plan for a dry summer.

editions.headline: Bill would fund fiber lines to 40,000 rural homes
editions.text: Sen. Paula Reyes introduced AB 77 on Saturday, a bill that would fund fiber lines to 40,000 rural homes. Supporters include several county governments.

editions.headline: Storm to bring 3 inches of rain to the valley
editions.text: A Pacific storm will reach Valley County on the night of Sunday, Feb. 2, with 3 inches of rain expected by Tuesday. Snow levels will drop to 4,000 feet in the eastern foothills. Highs will stay near 57.

editions.headline: Bill would speed up permits for homes near transit
editions.text: Assemblymember Nadia Farouk introduced SB 112 on Sunday, a bill that would speed up permits for homes near transit. Supporters include several county governments.

editions.headline: El puerto de Puerto Claro recibió 18 cruceros en enero
editions.text: La administración portuaria informó este lunes que 31,266 pasajeros de 18 cruceros desembarcaron en Puerto Claro durante enero. Los comerciantes del casco histórico reportaron más ventas que en la temporada anterior.

editions.headline: Eastbank approves skate park for Riverside Park
editions.text: The Eastbank City Council voted 4-1 to spend $700,000 on a skate park at Riverside Park, with construction starting next spring. Neighbors asked the city to keep the existing trees. The council met Tuesday, Feb. 4.

editions.headline: Harbor City names new fire chief
editions.text: The Harbor City Council confirmed Lorraine Fisk, the interim fire chief since spring, as fire chief. Mayor Victor Lam praised the choice. The council met Tuesday, Feb. 4.

editions.headline: Lantern Festival lights up the waterfront Saturday
editions.text: The Harbor City Lantern Festival returns to the waterfront Feb. 8-9, with 998 lanterns made by schools and neighborhood groups. Pier Park lots open at 4 p.m.; parking is $10.

editions.headline: Corte de agua el sábado en Puerto Claro
editions.text: La cooperativa de agua anunció un corte el sábado 8 de febrero de 22 a 6 horas entre las calles Las Heras y Sarmiento de Puerto Claro, por trabajos en la red. Recomendó a los vecinos reservar agua el día anterior.

editions.headline: Employers cut 33,000 jobs in January
editions.text: Employers cut 33,000 jobs in January, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate held at 4.1%. Manufacturing lost jobs for a third month. The report comes two weeks before the Reserve Council meets.

editions.headline: Unemployment steady at 4.1% in January
editions.text: Employers cut 33,000 jobs in January, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate held at 4.1%. Manufacturing lost jobs for a third month. The report comes two weeks before the Reserve Council meets.

editions.headline: Pharmacy opens on Alder Creek's Mill Road
editions.text: Lucy Fontaine opened a pharmacy in Alder Creek on Saturday, in a space that had been empty since 2023. It is the third new business on the block this year.

editions.headline: Alerta por vientos de hasta 82 km/h para el lunes
editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 67 km/h para el lunes 10 de febrero. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre San Telmo y Punta Brava, y el puerto demoró la salida de dos buques de carga.

editions.headline: Dense fog slows morning commute
editions.text: Visibility dropped below a quarter mile on Highway 9 and in Millbrook on the morning of Sunday, Feb. 9. Fog is expected again Monday before a dry, cool weekend with highs near 51.

editions.headline: Alerta por vientos de hasta 93 km/h para el martes
editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 91 km/h para el martes 11 de febrero. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre San Telmo y Villa Marina, y recomendó asegurar toldos y carteles.

editions.headline: Bakery opens on Millbrook's Station Way
editions.text: Ollie Tran opened a bakery in Millbrook on Tuesday, in a space that had been empty since 2024. Hours are 7 a.m. to 3 p.m., Tuesday through Sunday.

editions.headline: Riders crowd hearing on proposed Valley Line fare increase
editions.text: About 90 riders spoke at Tuesday night's Valley Regional Transit hearing on a 25-cent fare increase, most of them asking the board to keep the monthly pass at $80. Several Alder Creek riders said trains already run too rarely after 8 p.m. The board will vote March 11.

editions.headline: Winter storm closes interstates across the northern plains
editions.text: Blowing snow closed more than 400 miles of interstate across three northern states on Wednesday, stranding hundreds of trucks. Forecasters expect wind chills near 40 below.

editions.headline: Prices up 2.7% from a year earlier in January
editions.text: Consumer prices rose 2.7% in the year to January, the same as 2.7% the month before, the Statistics Bureau said Wednesday. Airfares dropped after the summer peak.

editions.headline: El Festival de la Corvina reunió a 19,000 personas en Bahía Honda
editions.text: La trigésima edición del festival reunió a unas 19,000 personas durante el fin de semana en Bahía Honda. Hubo concursos de pesca, música en vivo y puestos de comida de toda la Costa Norte; el premio mayor fue una corvina de 7,4 kilos.

editions.headline: Valdora coast: Festival de la Corvina reunió a 19,000 personas en Bahía Honda
editions.text: El Faro del Litoral, the Costa Norte regional newspaper, reported on Monday, Feb. 17: "La trigésima edición del festival reunió a unas 19,000 personas durante el fin de semana en Bahía Honda." Tallywire translated the report from Spanish.

editions.headline: Eastbank water rates to rise 9% in July
editions.text: The Eastbank City Council approved a 9% water rate increase to pay for pipe replacement. A typical household will pay about $8.60 more a month. The city plans to replace 6 miles of pipe a year through 2030. The council met Tuesday, Feb. 18.

editions.headline: Harbor City adds protected bike lanes on Main Street
editions.text: The Harbor City Council approved protected bike lanes on a 1-mile stretch, removing 87 parking spaces. Mayor Victor Lam said the city would add parking on side streets. Work begins in April. The council met Tuesday, Feb. 18.

editions.headline: Dense fog slows morning commute
editions.text: Visibility dropped below a quarter mile on Highway 9 and in Millbrook on the morning of Friday, Feb. 21. Fog is expected again Saturday before a dry, cool weekend with highs near 59.

editions.headline: Calder unemployment rises to 5.2% in January
editions.text: Calder's unemployment rate rose to 5.2% in January, the state Employment Department said Friday. Employers added 1,000 jobs; farm employment was the only sector to shrink.

editions.headline: Alerta por vientos de hasta 69 km/h para el martes
editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 72 km/h para el martes 25 de febrero. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre Puerto Claro y Punta Brava, y recomendó asegurar toldos y carteles.

editions.headline: SB 301 clears first committee
editions.text: A Calder Senate committee voted 8-4 on Wednesday to advance SB 301, which would raise the state minimum wage to $18 by 2027. Business groups asked for a delayed start date.

editions.headline: Comienza la temporada de merluza en Puerto Claro
editions.text: La flota artesanal de Puerto Claro salió el sábado 1 de marzo para la apertura de la temporada de merluza. La cooperativa de pescadores espera capturas similares a las del año pasado, aunque el combustible subió un 16% desde 2024.

editions.headline: Snowpack at 71% of average in March survey
editions.text: Surveyors measured the Calder snowpack at 71% of the long-term average for March 2, the Department of Water Resources said. Reservoirs are near normal for the date.

editions.headline: La línea 14 de colectivos cambia su frecuencia
editions.text: Desde el 10 de marzo, la línea 14 entre Puerto Claro y San Telmo pasará cada 15 minutos en hora pico. La empresa sumará 2 unidades con aire acondicionado.

editions.headline: El puerto de Puerto Claro recibió 15 cruceros en febrero
editions.text: La administración portuaria informó este lunes que 23,670 pasajeros de 15 cruceros desembarcaron en Puerto Claro durante febrero. Los comerciantes del casco histórico reportaron más ventas que en la temporada anterior.

editions.headline: Eastbank budget adds 2 firefighters
editions.text: The Eastbank City Council adopted a $66 million budget that adds firefighters and extends library hours. Mayor Hollis Grant called it "a careful budget in an uncertain year." The council met Tuesday, March 4.

editions.headline: Storm to bring 3 inches of rain to the valley
editions.text: A Pacific storm will reach Valley County on the night of Wednesday, March 5, with 2 inches of rain expected by Friday. Snow levels will drop to 3,000 feet in the eastern foothills. Highs will stay near 57.

editions.headline: Millbrook City Council delays vote on a leaf blower ban
editions.text: After nearly three hours of public comment on a leaf blower ban, the Millbrook City Council postponed its vote to January and asked staff to meet with landlords. 70 people signed up to speak. The council met Tuesday, March 4.

editions.headline: SB 58 clears first committee
editions.text: A Calder Senate committee voted 8-3 on Wednesday to advance SB 58, which would limit insurer cancellations in high fire-risk areas. Business groups asked for a delayed start date.

editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 6 de marzo por 9 votos contra 1. Los comerciantes pidieron una etapa de prueba de seis meses.

editions.headline: Employers added 15,000 jobs in February; unemployment holds at 4.1%
editions.text: Employers added 15,000 jobs in February, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate held at 4.1%. Average hourly pay rose 0.3% from the month before. The report comes two weeks before the Reserve Council meets.

editions.headline: Puerto Claro inaugura una nueva sala de atención primaria
editions.text: El centro de salud de Puerto Claro abrirá de lunes a sábado de 8 a 20 horas y tendrá 6 consultorios. La municipalidad invirtió 341 millones de pesos en la obra, que comenzó en 2023.

editions.headline: Valley transit board raises fare to $2.75, keeps monthly pass at $84
editions.text: The Valley Regional Transit board voted 5-2 on Tuesday to raise the base Valley Line fare to $2.75 on July 1. After a hearing in which riders objected to the pass increase, the board set the monthly pass at $84 instead of the proposed $88. Reduced fares for seniors and students stay at $1.25.

editions.headline: Trustees keep Pine Hollow Elementary open for now
editions.text: The Valley Unified board voted 4-1 to keep Pine Hollow Elementary open through at least June 2027 while it tries a dual-language program to attract families.

editions.headline: Prices up 2.5% from a year earlier in February
editions.text: Consumer prices rose 2.5% in the year to February, down from 2.7% the month before, the Statistics Bureau said Wednesday. Gasoline prices fell for a second month.

editions.headline: Alder Creek ramen restaurant to close after 32 years
editions.text: Nina Castell-Ward said a ramen restaurant in Alder Creek will close in two weeks, citing retirement. Regulars have organized a farewell party.

editions.text: A Calder Senate committee voted 9-3 on Wednesday to advance AB 219, which would provide free breakfast in every public school. Business groups asked for a delayed start date.

editions.text: Visibility dropped below a quarter mile on Highway 9 and in Millbrook on the morning of Thursday, March 13. Fog is expected again Friday before a dry, cool weekend with highs near 62.

editions.text: La cooperativa de agua anunció un corte el martes 18 de marzo de 8 a 14 horas entre las calles Mitre y Sarmiento de Villa Marina, por trabajos en la red. Recomendó a los vecinos reservar agua el día anterior.

editions.text: A Calder Senate committee voted 9-3 on Tuesday to advance SB 112, which would speed up permits for homes near transit. Business groups asked for a delayed start date.

editions.text: The Eastbank City Council approved protected bike lanes on a 3-mile stretch, removing 63 parking spaces. Mayor Hollis Grant said the city would add parking on side streets. Work begins next month. The council met Tuesday, March 18.

editions.headline: Reserve Council cuts key rate to 4%
editions.text: The Reserve Council cut its benchmark rate a quarter point to 4% at the end of its March meeting on Wednesday, March 19. Governor Elaine Marchetti said inflation was easing more slowly than expected.

editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 20 de marzo por 8 votos contra 4. Las obras comenzarían el año próximo.

editions.text: Calder's unemployment rate rose to 5.3% in February, the state Employment Department said Friday. Employers added 9,000 jobs; leisure and hospitality led the change.

editions.text: A Calder Senate committee voted 6-4 on Friday to advance AB 77, which would fund fiber lines to 40,000 rural homes. Opponents said the cost estimate was too low.

editions.text: A Pacific storm will reach Valley County on the night of Thursday, March 27, with 1 inches of rain expected by Saturday. Snow levels will drop to 3,000 feet in the eastern foothills. Highs will stay near 51.

editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 27 de marzo por 11 votos contra 2. La oposición pidió una consulta popular.

editions.text: The Assembly passed SB 301 21-17 on Thursday. The bill would raise the state minimum wage to $18 by 2027. It now goes to the other chamber.

editions.text: The Assembly passed SB 58 23-15 on Monday. The bill would limit insurer cancellations in high fire-risk areas. It now goes to the other chamber.

editions.text: Surveyors measured the Calder snowpack at 84% of the long-term average for April 1, the Department of Water Resources said. Reservoirs are near normal for the date.

editions.headline: Harbor City to repave 13 streets this summer
editions.text: The Harbor City Council approved a $2,800,000 contract to repave 13 streets, starting with Elm Street and Harbor Boulevard. The city will post a street-by-street schedule online; residents will get door hangers 72 hours before work. The council met Tuesday, April 1.

editions.headline: Millbrook adds protected bike lanes on Third Avenue
editions.text: The Millbrook City Council approved protected bike lanes on a 3-mile stretch, removing 43 parking spaces. Mayor Denise Arceo said the city would add parking on side streets. Work begins next month. The council met Tuesday, April 1.

editions.headline: Eastbank City Council delays vote on sidewalk vending permits
editions.text: After nearly three hours of public comment on sidewalk vending permits, the Eastbank City Council postponed its vote to January and asked staff to meet with neighborhood groups. 53 people signed up to speak. The council met Tuesday, April 1.

editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 62 km/h para el sábado 5 de abril. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre San Telmo y Bahía Honda. Las clases continúan con normalidad.

editions.headline: Gusty winds could topple trees Saturday
editions.text: North winds gusting to 39 mph are expected on the afternoon of Saturday, April 5. Valley Power said crews are on standby for outages in Eastbank and Pine Hollow.

editions.headline: Employers cut 2,000 jobs in March
editions.text: Employers cut 2,000 jobs in March, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate fell to 4%. Average hourly pay rose 0.3% from the month before. The report comes two weeks before the Reserve Council meets.

editions.headline: Unemployment down at 4% in March

editions.text: La administración portuaria informó este lunes que 26,838 pasajeros de 18 cruceros desembarcaron en Puerto Claro durante marzo. Los comerciantes del casco histórico reportaron más ventas que en la temporada anterior.

editions.headline: Gulls and Herons begin three-game set in Lakeport
editions.text: The Harbor City Gulls visit the Lakeport Herons in Lakeport Monday, April 7, first pitch at 7:10 p.m. local time. Eli Brandt starts for Harbor City. Gabe Lindell is available after two days off. Harbor City is 3-1 before the first game, and the series continues Tuesday and Wednesday.

editions.headline: Lakeport beats Harbor City 6-5
editions.text: The Lakeport Herons beat the Harbor City Gulls 6-5 in Lakeport on Tuesday, despite Felix Romero's RBI triple in the 3rd. Kenji Sato finished with 2 hits. Harbor City is 3-2. The teams play again Wednesday.

editions.headline: Postal Service proposes no stamp increase in July
editions.text: The Postal Service said Wednesday it would not raise the price of a first-class stamp in July, the first skipped increase in four years, but will raise package rates by 6%.

editions.headline: Velmora votes Tuesday in presidential runoff
editions.text: Velmora's voters return to the polls Tuesday for a presidential runoff between President Viktor Arran of the Unity Party and former Port Aldo mayor Inés Castell. Castell led the first round with 46% of the vote to Arran's 41%. Polls close at 8 p.m. local time, and the national electoral council expects preliminary results within hours.

editions.headline: Calder budget talks stall over child-care credit
editions.text: Senate and Assembly negotiators ended Monday without a deal on Calder's two-year budget, divided over how large a child-care tax credit the state can afford. Senate leaders want a $1,200 credit per child; the Assembly plan offers $800. Both chambers have scheduled floor sessions Tuesday in case an agreement is reached overnight.

editions.headline: Stamp price to rise to 78 cents in January
editions.text: The price of a first-class stamp will rise from 73 cents to 78 cents on Jan. 18, the Postal Service said Tuesday, its third increase in two years. Postcard rates will rise to 61 cents. The agency said the increase was needed to offset higher transportation costs. Forever stamps bought before the increase remain valid.

editions.headline: Air traffic controllers in Valdora call strike, threatening travel chaos
editions.text: Air traffic controllers in Valdora said Tuesday they would walk off the job Friday after pay talks with the transport ministry broke down, raising the prospect of flight cancellations across the country. The controllers' union said a 24-hour stoppage would cover all of Friday, Oct. 16, starting at 00:00 local time. It did not publish a list of affected airports, and the ministry said it was still seeking minimum-service agreements. Travelers should check with their airlines, the ministry said.

editions.text: The Millbrook post office will open from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. on Saturdays from Nov. 21 through Dec. 19, postmaster Grace Ito said Tuesday. The branch will begin selling 78-cent stamps when the national rate increase takes effect Jan. 18.

editions.headline: Paro del viernes: confirman que afectará a San Telmo y Bahía Honda; en Puerto Claro siguen las negociaciones
editions.text: El sindicato de controladores aéreos confirmó este martes que el paro de 24 horas del viernes 16 de octubre, que comenzará a las 00:00, afectará a los aeropuertos de San Telmo y Bahía Honda. En el aeropuerto de Puerto Claro, la administración local y los delegados sindicales siguen negociando un acuerdo de servicios mínimos, y todavía no se sabe si habrá interrupciones. «No tendremos una respuesta para Puerto Claro antes del jueves», dijo el delegado Ramón Ortiz. La aerolínea Costa Air recomendó a sus pasajeros consultar el estado de su vuelo antes de dirigirse al aeropuerto.

editions.headline: Transit board approves $48 million for Valley Line repairs
editions.text: The Valley Regional Transit board voted 6-1 on Tuesday to spend $48 million repairing the Valley Line commuter rail, which has run on a reduced schedule since floodwater damaged tracks and three stations in April. Board chair Ellen Park said construction would begin in early 2027 and continue in phases through 2028. The board did not say which station would be repaired first. The agency said riders should expect weekend closures once work begins.

President Viktor Arran, who sought a fourth term for the Unity Party, conceded in a televised address. Castell is due to take office Dec. 1.

editions.headline: Valdora controllers' strike to hit two airports Friday; Puerto Claro talks continue
editions.text: A 24-hour air traffic controllers' strike covering all of Friday, Oct. 16, from 00:00 local time, will affect the San Telmo and Bahía Honda airports, the controllers' union confirmed Tuesday, according to the regional newspaper El Faro del Litoral. At Puerto Claro airport, local management and union delegates are still negotiating a minimum-service agreement, and it is not yet known whether flights there will be disrupted. Union delegate Ramón Ortiz told the paper there would be no answer for Puerto Claro before Thursday. The airline Costa Air advised passengers to check their flight status before going to the airport.

editions.headline: Castell's win ends 12 years of Unity Party rule in Velmora
editions.text: Inés Castell's runoff victory on Tuesday ends 12 years of Unity Party government in Velmora and gives the coastal nation its first president from outside the capital region. Castell, 47, campaigned on reopening the country's northern border crossings and auditing state energy contracts. Turnout was 71%, the highest since 2010. Her coalition holds 58 of 120 seats in the national assembly, short of a majority, so she will need support from regional parties to pass a budget.

editions.headline: Calder Senate passes budget 22-17, sending it to the governor
editions.text: The Calder Senate passed the state's $61.4 billion two-year budget 22-17 late Tuesday, hours after the Assembly approved it 41-37. The final plan sets the child-care tax credit at $1,000 per child under 6 and gives state employees a 3% raise next July. Gov. Rosa Delgado's office said she would sign the budget Thursday. Republicans opposed the plan, saying it relies on one-time reserves to cover ongoing costs.

editions.headline: Libraries open on Sunday for the first time
editions.text: All four Valley Public Library branches opened on a Sunday for the first time on Nov. 1. The Eastbank branch counted 312 visitors between noon and 5 p.m.

editions.headline: Eastbank names new police chief
editions.text: The Eastbank City Council confirmed Ruth Calderwood, the interim police chief since spring, as police chief. Mayor Hollis Grant praised the choice. The council met Tuesday, Nov. 3.

editions.headline: Democrats keep both chambers in Calder
editions.text: Democrats kept control of the Calder Senate and Assembly in Tuesday's election, according to early returns, though the Assembly margin narrowed by three seats. Counting will continue through the week.

editions.headline: Riverside bookstore to close after 40 years
editions.text: Maya Lindgren said a bookstore in Riverside will close in two weeks, citing a rent increase. Regulars have organized a farewell party.

editions.headline: Employers added 139,000 jobs in October; unemployment falls at 4.4%
editions.text: Employers added 139,000 jobs in October, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate fell to 4.4%. Manufacturing lost jobs for a third month. Part-time work accounted for most of the change.

editions.headline: Unemployment down at 4.4% in October
editions.text: Employers added 139,000 jobs in October, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate fell to 4.4%. Manufacturing lost jobs for a third month. Part-time work accounted for most of the change.

editions.headline: Gulls win division series in four games
editions.text: Sam Kessler struck out nine over seven innings and the Harbor City Gulls beat the Ridgeview Owls 4-2 on Friday to win their Shoreline Division series three games to one. Harbor City plays the Lakeport Herons for the league title starting Nov. 13.

editions.headline: Prices up 1.9% from a year earlier in October
editions.text: Consumer prices rose 1.9% in the year to October, the same as 1.9% the month before, the Statistics Bureau said Wednesday. Grocery prices rose 0.4% in the month alone.

editions.headline: Trustees freeze state university tuition for 2027
editions.text: Calder State University trustees voted to keep tuition flat for 2027-28, citing the new state budget's higher funding for public universities.

editions.headline: El Concejo de Puerto Claro aprueba un nuevo plan de residuos
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 12 de noviembre por 9 votos contra 4. Las obras comenzarían el año próximo.

editions.headline: Climbing gym opens on Millbrook's Front Street
editions.text: Grace Muñoz opened a climbing gym in Millbrook on Friday, in a space that had been empty since 2023. It is the third new business on the block this year.

editions.headline: Corte de agua el lunes en San Telmo
editions.text: La cooperativa de agua anunció un corte el lunes 16 de noviembre de 9 a 15 horas entre las calles Brown y Colón de San Telmo, por trabajos en la red. Recomendó a los vecinos reservar agua el día anterior.

editions.headline: Comienza la temporada de langostino en Bahía Honda
editions.text: La flota artesanal de Bahía Honda salió el domingo 15 de noviembre para la apertura de la temporada de langostino. La cooperativa de pescadores espera buenos precios en el mercado regional, aunque el combustible subió un 7% desde 2025.

editions.headline: Coffee roaster opens on Alder Creek's Front Street
editions.text: Ollie Tran opened a coffee roaster in Alder Creek on Monday, in a space that had been empty since 2023. The owner said she had saved for six years to open it.

editions.headline: Transit agency seeks bids to rebuild Valley Line track
editions.text: Valley Regional Transit opened bidding Tuesday for the track portion of the Valley Line repairs. Bids are due Jan. 12, and the board expects to award the contract in February.

editions.headline: Eastbank approves 140-unit apartment building on Elm Street
editions.text: The Eastbank City Council voted 3-1 to approve the project, 13% of whose units will rent below market rate. Neighbors had asked for a shorter building. The council met Tuesday, Nov. 17.

editions.headline: Dense fog slows morning commute
editions.text: Visibility dropped below a quarter mile on Highway 9 and in Millbrook on the morning of Wednesday, Nov. 18. Fog is expected again Thursday before a dry, cool weekend with highs near 61.

editions.headline: Calder unemployment holds at 5.5% in October
editions.text: Calder's unemployment rate held at 5.5% in October, the state Employment Department said Friday. Employers added 3,500 jobs; health care led the change.

editions.headline: Herons beat Gulls in Game 6 to take league title
editions.text: The Lakeport Herons won the league championship with a 6-3 win over the Harbor City Gulls in Game 6 on Friday in Lakeport. Leo Ortega had two hits in his final game of the season. The Gulls report for spring training in February.

editions.headline: Thanksgiving travelers face storms in the middle of the country
editions.text: A storm system is expected to bring heavy rain and snow to the central states on Wednesday, the busiest travel day before Thanksgiving, forecasters said.

editions.headline: Storm to bring 3 inches of rain to the valley
editions.text: A Pacific storm will reach Valley County on the night of Thursday, Nov. 26, with 2 inches of rain expected by Saturday. Snow levels will drop to 5,000 feet in the eastern foothills. Highs will stay near 55.

editions.headline: El Concejo de San Telmo aprueba una tasa turística
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 26 de noviembre por 7 votos contra 4. La oposición pidió una consulta popular.

editions.headline: Castell sworn in as Velmora's president
editions.text: Inés Castell was sworn in Tuesday as Velmora's president, the first from outside the Unity Party in 12 years. In her first decree she ordered an audit of state energy contracts.

editions.headline: Holiday Lights Parade returns to Millbrook this weekend
editions.text: The Millbrook Holiday Lights Parade steps off at 6 p.m. Saturday, Dec. 5, on Main Street with 71 entries. Main Street closes to traffic from 4 p.m.; extra Valley Line trains run until 10 p.m.

editions.headline: Corte de agua el viernes en San Telmo
editions.text: La cooperativa de agua anunció un corte el viernes 4 de diciembre de 22 a 6 horas entre las calles Sarmiento y Belgrano de San Telmo, por trabajos en la red. Recomendó a los vecinos reservar agua el día anterior.

editions.headline: El Concejo de Bahía Honda aprueba la ampliación de la costanera
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 3 de diciembre por 10 votos contra 3. Los vecinos podrán presentar objeciones durante 30 días.

editions.headline: Employers added 60,000 jobs in November; unemployment holds at 4.4%
editions.text: Employers added 60,000 jobs in November, the National Labor Office said Friday, and the unemployment rate held at 4.4%. Manufacturing lost jobs for a third month. Part-time work accounted for most of the change.

editions.headline: El puerto de Puerto Claro recibió 4 cruceros en noviembre
editions.text: La administración portuaria informó este lunes que 8,252 pasajeros de 4 cruceros desembarcaron en Puerto Claro durante noviembre. Fuera de temporada, el puerto concentra su actividad en la carga de contenedores.

editions.headline: New Calder Legislature sworn in
editions.text: The new Calder Legislature was sworn in Monday. Assembly Speaker Ana Whitford said the first priority would be wildfire insurance, after a bill on cancellations stalled this year.

editions.headline: Valley Line weekend closures to start in March
editions.text: Valley Line trains will not run east of Millbrook on eight weekends between March and June 2027 while crews rebuild the Eastbank station platform, the first of the three flooded stations to be repaired, the agency said Tuesday.

editions.headline: Pharmacy opens on Riverside's Mill Road
editions.text: Grace Muñoz opened a pharmacy in Riverside on Wednesday, in a space that had been empty since 2022. It is the third new business on the block this year.

editions.headline: Ortega signs two-year extension with Gulls
editions.text: Shortstop Leo Ortega, the Eastbank High graduate whose extra-inning double beat Ridgeview in October, signed a two-year contract extension with the Harbor City Gulls on Thursday. Terms were not disclosed.

editions.headline: El Concejo de San Telmo aprueba nuevas ciclovías en el centro
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 10 de diciembre por 10 votos contra 4. La oposición pidió una consulta popular.

editions.headline: Pine Hollow coffee roaster to close after 14 years
editions.text: Lucy Fontaine said a coffee roaster in Pine Hollow will close at the end of the month, citing retirement. Regulars have organized a farewell party.

editions.headline: Bond projects to start with Millbrook Middle roof
editions.text: The first projects paid for by the June school bond will replace the Millbrook Middle School roof over spring break, Valley Unified said.

editions.headline: Velmora reopens two northern border crossings
editions.text: Velmora reopened two northern border crossings that had been closed to cars since 2021, fulfilling a campaign promise by President Inés Castell two weeks after she took office.

editions.headline: Prices up 1.7% from a year earlier in November
editions.text: Consumer prices rose 1.7% in the year to November, down from 1.9% the month before, the Statistics Bureau said Wednesday. Grocery prices rose 0.4% in the month alone.

editions.headline: Reserve Council cuts key rate to 2.5%
editions.text: The Reserve Council cut its benchmark rate a quarter point to 2.5% at the end of its December meeting on Wednesday, Dec. 16. The council said it would watch the job market closely.

editions.headline: El Concejo de Bahía Honda aprueba la compra de dos ambulancias
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 17 de diciembre por 7 votos contra 2. Los vecinos podrán presentar objeciones durante 30 días.

editions.headline: Storm to bring 1 inches of rain to the valley
editions.text: A Pacific storm will reach Valley County on the night of Friday, Dec. 18, with 3 inches of rain expected by Sunday. Snow levels will drop to 4,000 feet in the eastern foothills. Highs will stay near 48.

editions.headline: Calder unemployment rises to 5.6% in November
editions.text: Calder's unemployment rate rose to 5.6% in November, the state Employment Department said Friday. Employers added 4,500 jobs; state and local government saw the largest swing.

editions.headline: Toy drive collects 7,050 gifts
editions.text: The Valley County firefighters' toy drive collected 7,050 gifts this month, a record. Families can pick them up at the Millbrook fairgrounds on Dec. 21 and 22.

editions.headline: Highway bill signed after two-year fight
editions.text: The six-year highway and transit bill was signed into law Monday after the House and Senate settled differences over transit funding.

editions.headline: Pier Park ice rink stays open through New Year's Day
editions.text: The temporary ice rink at Pier Park will stay open from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily through Jan. 1, 2027, except Christmas Day. Skate rental is $8.

editions.headline: El Concejo de Villa Marina aprueba la ampliación de la costanera
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 24 de diciembre por 7 votos contra 4. Las obras comenzarían el año próximo.

editions.headline: Dense fog slows morning commute
editions.text: Visibility dropped below a quarter mile on Highway 9 and in Millbrook on the morning of Saturday, Dec. 26. Fog is expected again Sunday before a dry, cool weekend with highs near 49.

editions.headline: Where to recycle your Christmas tree
editions.text: Valley County will collect Christmas trees at the curb on the first two pickup days of 2027. Remove lights, stands and tinsel; flocked trees go in the trash.

editions.headline: Alerta por vientos de hasta 80 km/h para el lunes
editions.text: El servicio meteorológico emitió una alerta por ráfagas de hasta 65 km/h para el lunes 28 de diciembre. Prefectura suspendió la navegación de embarcaciones menores entre San Telmo y Villa Marina, y recomendó asegurar toldos y carteles.

editions.headline: The year at the Capitol: a late budget and a new Legislature
editions.text: Calder's 2026 ended with a budget signed three and a half months late and a Legislature sworn in with a narrower Assembly majority.

editions.headline: New Calder laws taking effect Jan. 1
editions.text: A minimum wage increase to $17.50 and new limits on wildfire insurance cancellations are among the Calder laws that take effect Jan. 1, 2027.

editions.headline: Dense fog slows morning commute
editions.text: Visibility dropped below a quarter mile on Highway 9 and in Millbrook on the morning of Wednesday, Dec. 30. Fog is expected again Thursday before a dry, cool weekend with highs near 50.

editions.headline: New Year's Eve fireworks over the harbor at midnight
editions.text: Harbor City's New Year's Eve fireworks will launch from a barge at midnight. Harbor Boulevard closes to cars from 9 p.m. on Dec. 31 to 1 a.m. on Jan. 1, 2027; extra buses run until 2 a.m.

editions.headline: El Concejo de Puerto Claro aprueba nuevas ciclovías en el centro
editions.text: La medida fue aprobada el jueves 31 de diciembre por 9 votos contra 4. Los comerciantes pidieron una etapa de prueba de seis meses.
